headline: A lingering offshore low keeps showers and cool weather through Friday, then a mostly dry, chilly weekend follows into midweek.
summary: As of Wednesday evening, a pocket of cold air high in the atmosphere (an upper-level low) sits just offshore and won't move much through Friday. It keeps western Washington unsettled, with scattered showers in the lowlands and light snow in the Cascades. Highs on Thursday and Friday should be in the low to mid 50s. Rain totals are trending down, and much of the area may stay somewhat dry between showers, though stray showers can't be ruled out. Wednesday's small thunderstorm chance (15 to 20%) was expected to drop sharply after sunset, and Cascade snow showers had faded a lot since the morning, with most of the snow falling in and around Mount Rainier. The Cascades Winter Weather Advisory ended at 5 PM Wednesday, and no land-based alerts remain. Over the weekend the low weakens and conditions turn drier, with highs around the mid 50s. Nights get colder, with lows in the low to mid 30s, and a few spots, especially the Southwest Interior, could drop to the mid to upper 20s. A weak upper-level ridge (a area of higher pressure aloft) should keep things likely dry into the middle of next week. Forecasters are fairly confident the low weakens and the weather dries out, but less certain about exactly where showers pop up Thursday and Friday. Small craft advisories for steep seas along the coast and the Grays Harbor Bar ended Wednesday night, mainly of concern to boaters.
changes: The early-morning discussion mentioned patchy fog Monday and Tuesday and a possible north-coast clip from a warm front, but later discussions dropped those and simply called for dry weather into midweek. Snow in the Cascades also ended up much lighter than first expected, and the advisory expired on schedule.
